questions.question: Which description fits the **EpisodeOfCare** resource?
options: An association between a patient and an organization / healthcare provider(s) during which time encounters may occur.
Prospective warnings of potential issues when providing care to the patient.
This resource is a general-purpose container for knowledge asset definitions.
An interaction between a patient and healthcare provider(s) for the purpose of providing healthcare service(s) or assessing the health status of a patient.
questions.explanation: **EpisodeOfCare**: An association between a patient and an organization / healthcare provider(s) during which time encounters may occur. The managing organization assumes a level of responsibility for the patient during this time. The other descriptions belong to **Flag**, **Library**, **Encounter**.

questions.question: Which resource would you use? All the care a woman receives during her pregnancy, across many visits.
questions.explanation: **EpisodeOfCare**. Groups encounters over a period of responsibility for a condition. One episode, many encounters.

questions.question: You know **EpisodeOfCare**. Which resource should you use instead when you need “what is planned, not the period of responsibility”?
questions.explanation: **CarePlan**: what is planned, not the period of responsibility. **EpisodeOfCare** is for something else: An association between a patient and an organization / healthcare provider(s) during which time encounters may occur.

questions.question: Which element is **required** (minimum cardinality 1) in every **EpisodeOfCare** instance?
questions.explanation: The required top-level elements of EpisodeOfCare are `status` (1..1), `patient` (1..1). The other options have a minimum cardinality of 0, so they are optional.

questions.question: Which element of **EpisodeOfCare** is a **modifier** (?!), so receiving systems must not ignore it?
questions.explanation: Modifier elements of EpisodeOfCare: `status`. `status`: planned | waitlist | active | onhold | finished | cancelled | entered-in-error. A modifier can change the meaning of the whole resource: for example, a status of `entered-in-error` means the data must not be used.
